rationale: Three lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) ran against the real functional diff: docs/ARCHITECTURE-OTLP-PLUGIN.md (one table-row update), session-signals.ts + its tests, and claude-named-invocations.ts + its tests. The branch-vs-base diff also adds ~800 lines of docs/superpowers/tasks/2026-11-16-session-summary-turns-regression/* process artifacts (prior sdlc-light run's plan.md, qa-report.md, technical-analysis.md, actual-complexity.json, decisions.jsonl, events.jsonl, gate-plan.json, and the embedded prior code-review.diff/code-review-check.diff/code-review-final.json/code-review-check.json) — these are non-functional bookkeeping, not implementation, so they were excluded from lens review and are not re-litigated here. One new blocking finding survived triage (CR-001, major/patch): nextSkillName()'s forward lookahead in claude-named-invocations.ts (extended by the third, not-yet-reviewed commit 'widen skill-dedup lookahead past prep tool_use round-trips') only skips isMeta/isSidechain lines, not other housekeeping lines that carry no `message` field at all (e.g. a `compact_boundary` system line) — confirmed via transcript-lines.ts that isCountedTranscriptLine() lets such lines through unfiltered into the messages array this function scans. Such a line forces nextSkillName's premature `return ''`, which can reproduce the exact EPMCDME-17201 double-count bug in the narrow window where auto-compaction (or any other message-less system line) falls between a skill-backed slash command and its Skill tool_use reply — the same class of gap as the prior round's CR-001, just a different housekeeping-line shape the earlier fix-up didn't anticipate. EPMCDME-15582's four story ACs and the plan's Global Constraints/Review Focus are all satisfied and covered by new tests. EPMCDME-17201 AC3 (no Tools & Models double-count) is satisfied: confirmed by reading the full current file that the unconditional skillInvocations bump (lines 192-203, untouched by this diff) runs independently of recordCommand's dedup, so the skill side is always counted exactly once regardless of the dedup outcome; the acceptance lens's own 'partial' call on this item is overridden here with direct evidence. EPMCDME-17201 ACs 1/2/5 and its three requested regression-test categories (backend _dispatch_label_and_kind() unit tests, mixed slash/Skill integration tests, a UI timeline-bar test) are correctly `na`: per the ticket's own description and this plan's explicit 'client-side only' Global Constraint, that classification/timeline logic lives in a different, backend/UI-owned codebase, not this repo — same situation as EPMCDME-15582's already-shipped backend rollup half. Eight other lens concerns were triaged to dismiss (not emitted, counted here): (1) nextSkillName's forward scan not terminating on a plain-text-only assistant reply with no tool_use at all — traced and found unreachable in practice, since the next transcript line after such a reply is always either a housekeeping line (now also handled once CR-001 is fixed) or a genuine new user message, both of which correctly terminate the scan; a defensive nice-to-have, not a correctness gap; (2) O(n) nested forward-scan cost per recorded command — realistic sessions have at most tens of slash commands, not a real performance risk; (3) duplicate identical command tags inside one message sharing one lookahead result — an unrealistic transcript shape the CLI does not produce; (4) wrappedCommandName returning only the first match — intentional, documented, matches the codebase's own one-command-per-turn invariant; (5) case-sensitivity mismatch between wrappedCommandName's output and LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS — command names are CLI-literal and always lower-case, never user-typed with mixed case; (6) cross-plugin import of claude-named-invocations.ts into session-signals.ts — no project guide forbids this, and ARCHITECTURE-OTLP-PLUGIN.md already documents the cross-reference explicitly; (7) LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS not also applied to commandInvocations/slash-command counts — a different metric, not required by either ticket's acceptance criteria; (8) the documented cross-repo SENTINEL_EXACT drift risk — an already-accepted, explicitly-documented design tradeoff carried over from the prior review round. One further blind-lens item ('no-op diff hunk') was discarded entirely (not counted as dismiss): verified directly against `git diff` and confirmed to be a transcription artifact introduced while excerpting the diff for the blind-lens dispatch prompt, not a real issue in the repository.

findings.title: nextSkillName stops at message-less housekeeping lines
findings.problem: nextSkillName's forward scan skips only `isMeta`/`isSidechain` lines before checking role; a line with no `message` field at all (e.g. a `compact_boundary` system line, which `isCountedTranscriptLine()` in transcript-lines.ts lets through unfiltered) has `role === undefined`, so the `if (role !== 'assistant') return '';` guard fires and ends the scan early.
findings.impact: If such a message-less housekeeping line falls between a skill-backed slash command and the assistant's matching Skill tool_use call (plausible if auto-compaction triggers mid-turn), the lookahead wrongly returns '' and the command is double-counted as both a command and a skill — reproducing the exact EPMCDME-17201 bug this change exists to fix, in a transcript shape none of the new tests exercise.
findings.recommendation: Treat a message with no `message.role` of 'user'/'assistant' the same as an isMeta/isSidechain line (skip and continue scanning) instead of returning '' — e.g. `if (role == null) continue;` before the `role !== 'assistant'` check — and add a test with an interposed `compact_boundary`-shaped line (no `message` field) between the command and the Skill call.
